content.comment_body: Hello everyone! My setup consists of two [product_name] main modules and four expansion modules, configured with one acting as master and the other as slave, both connected via network. I’m trying to control the outputs on the slave from the master using network inputs. Currently, I set parameters to read values from the remote device, specifying its IP address and device type ([product_name] slave), along with the relevant block type and block number. The issue is that network input only supports 32 slots for data transfer, but I have 20 outputs on each device—40 in total. Is there any way to use all 40 outputs from the master project? Attached is the related error. Thank you for reading! [document] M.
Welcome to the forum. Do you need to use a master/slave communication? You would have more options and flexibility by using a master/master (client/server) communication instead.
Thank you for your quick response! Could you please provide some guidance on how, in a master/master setup, the devices can access each other's outputs and inputs? What instructions should I use?
I recommend creating a network project and adding both [product_name] devices to it. You can import your previous master configuration. Would you like a demonstration to get started?
That would be fantastic. If possible, could you share an example where an input on one device activates an output on the other?
Alright, I'll prepare an example for you. Please be patient—it may not be ready today, but you’ll definitely have it tomorrow.
Remember to take the former slave [product_name] out of slave mode.
Thank you! I’ll try testing this later. I really appreciate your help!

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced a limitation with data transfer slots (maximum 32) when implementing network inputs in a master/slave configuration between two [product_name] modules. This prevented control of all 40 outputs as planned, revealing a scalability constraint. Community members suggested switching to a network project utilizing a master/master (client/server) approach, which may offer increased flexibility and help overcome such limits.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to control all 40 outputs across two [product_name] devices over the network without encountering restrictions related to data transfer limits.
